preview: Interview experience for JPMC on-campus hiring through Code for Good 2023, detailing the online coding test, HireVue video interview, hackathon rounds, and preparation tips.
content: Shaurya Swarup B.Tech CS INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE On-campus Hiring JPMC on-campus hiring for summer internship and FTE happens every year via Code for Good which is a 2-day hackathon. Teams are supposed to collaborate to create tech solutions for nonprofit challenges. It promotes tech innovation for social good, connecting participants with mentors and nonprofit partners. Eligibility Criteria: ❖Degrees: B.Tech./B.E./MCA ❖Streams or Specializations: Computer Science/Information Science/ Information Technology/Data Science/Artificial Intelligence/Big Data/IoT/Electronics/ Electrical/Electronics and Telecommunications etc. ❖Minimum aggregate 7 CGPA [until date of registration] in engineering course Timeline: ❖Registration Process: 10th March to 23rd March ❖Online Coding Test: 10th April ❖Video Interview: Deadline 17th April ❖Code for Good Shortlist announcement: 6th June ❖Code for Good Event: 15th and 16th July ❖Internship Shortlist announcement: 28th August Coding Round (60 minutes) The online coding test conducted on HackerRank platform is the first step in the SEP selection process. This is a programming test of 100 marks having 2 programming questions carrying 50 marks each. The time allowed for this test is 60 Minutes. Following were the questions I had in the coding round: ❖Maximum Index I took around 20-25 minutes to solve this problem. I could solve all the test cases. It is a greedy problem, does not require any knowledge of DSA to be honest, just some observation and understanding. Give it a go before reading my approach. Problem Maximum index a pointer can reach in N steps by avoiding a given index B - GeeksforGeeks There is an infinite array of integers numbered consecutively from 0. At each step, a pointer can move from index i to index i+j, or remain where it is. The value of i begins at 0. The value of j begins at 1 and at each step, j increments by 1. There is one known index that must be avoided. Determine the highest index that can be reached in a given number of steps. Example steps = 4 badElement = 6 The pointer is limited to 4 steps and should avoid the bad item 6. ● Scenario 1: ○ In the first step, j starts at 1. ○ Move 1 unit to index 0+1=1 and j=2. ○ At step 2, move 2 units to index 1+2-3, and j=3. ○ At step 3, do not move. Otherwise point moves 3 units to bad item 6. Now j=4. ○ At step 4, move 4 units to item 3+4=7. ● Scenario 2: ○ At step 1, remain at index 0. Now j=2. ○ At step 2, move 2 units to index 0+2-2 and j=3. ○ At step 3, move 3 units to index 2+3=5 and j=4 ○ At step 4, move 4 units to index 5+4=9 The maximum index that can be reached is 9. >> First line of input shows the number of steps. Second line is the index of the bad element. Sample Input 2 2 Sample Output 3 Explanation: Move 2 steps and avoid index number 2. At step 1 move 1 unit to step 0+1=1. At step 2, move 2 units to step 1+2=3. The maximum index that can be reached is 3. ❖Counting Bits: https://www.codingninjas.com/studio/library/count-number-of-set-bits-in-an-integer The question had one more part to it. I don’t exactly remember what it was though. But it was fairly simple. Just needed to use a hash map (that’s all that I can recollect). Comparable to a Leetcode easy to medium question. Again, solved all the test cases. (Not gonna lie, it did take me 20-25 minutes to debug my code for 4 large input test cases, but it was because at some point I had to use a multiset and not a set, because of duplicate inputs, yes I just had to add 5 letters “m-u-l-t-i” to my data structure definition 🙂). Video Interview (10 minutes) The next step of the recruiting process is a video interview, powered by HireVue. In this HireVue interview, you will be asked to record video responses to 2 interview questions. The types of questions in video interviews are pretty standard, some of them are: ❖Where do you see your career in 10 years? ❖What are your achievements and what learning did you get from the same? ❖Talk about a recent experience where you learnt a lot. Pretty standard questions. I chose to talk about my hackathon experience in questions related to my experiences and my lessons. Just google HireVue questions online and you’ll get a list of questions and good answers for the same. Also, worth noting, there is an option to re-record your response once for each question. If you re-record any response that will be automatically submitted as the final response for that question. Link to practice: HireVue Digital Interviews Shortlist Results The final list of all shortlisted students came out about a month later from the video interview submission, 10 students were selected for the hackathon. Code for Good 2023 Hackathon (15th and 16th) The hackathon for my batch was conducted online. During hackathon: The event kicked off with an introduction to the company. They talked about the company overview, mission and vision, core values and culture, industry position, career development and growth opportunities, employee benefits and perks and social initiatives taken up by JPMC. It would be advisable to not skip this since there might be questions regarding the company in one-on-one with the mentors. After that, the CFG coordinators introduced the non-profit organizations, their problem statements, and requirements to all the participants. Following these presentations, all teams were given time to discuss their order of preference for the problem statements. A form was then made available, requiring us to indicate our preferences. The assignment of problem statements to each group was done on a first-come, first-serve basis according to the order of form submissions. (So I took up the responsibility of submitting our topic preference, and I did this so fast – took me 5 seconds, that we were the first team to be allotted the topic of our choice 😂.) A zoom meeting with our mentors (I had two) was scheduled, it is quite important to be present in that zoom meeting throughout the event. There were two one-on-one sessions with the mentors during the hackathon. They were approximately 15 minutes long, where each mentor asked me questions. They started off by trying to make me comfortable and talk in general. Questions with Mentor 1 (He was not a technical person at all, which he himself told us, so he asked me behavioral and situational questions) in session one (evening): 1. How is the team doing? What is the progress of the project? 2. Are you planning for further studies after college? 3. How was I finding it working with the team and technologies? 4. What are your interests, and what would you do if you were not a programmer? 5. [Situational Question] If you were given 3 choices →Work alone, Work in a team, Lead a team, what would you choose? Questions with Mentor 2 (He was a technical person so asked me accordingly) in session two (midnight): 1. What is the project status? 2. What are your contributions, what features are you developing? Now I had created the entire backend (Auth+Database+Controllers+API Routes), so he started asking me why am I making an API with regards to the problem statement of the hackathon 3. Why an API? Why not just a normal backend server processing queries? 4. What database are you using, why? They ended the discussion by asking me if I had any questions for them. I asked how the work culture is in JPMC and what they expect from interns. My tips for the hackathon: ● Take initiative, do not wait for others to mess something up and then tell them. ● Be quick and prompt in decision making, and split work according to the skillset of members. ● Your team members may not know all the technologies you work with (they might just know HTML & CSS) but still divide the work in order to get things done. ● Voice your opinions clearly and make sure there is constant communication between ALL team members. This is the most crucial piece of advice. ● You do not need to win the hackathon in order to secure an internship. You may not get an internship even if you win the hackathon. But you need to show throughout the hackathon that you are a good team player, and developer. We did not win the hackathon, but 6 out of 7 of my teammates (including me) secured an internship, which is a rare feat, and this is only because our team work was incredibly smooth, and we had effective communication and collaboration. Internship Offer After 1 month, the internship selections were announced, 5 out of 10 received internship offers, and all 5 accepted the offer since the results were announced before the arrival of any other company in the college. Tips Even though I did not have a conventional interview like most do, I did keep working on myself for 2 months until I got the internship offer… So these tips are not exactly just limited to JPMC but for internship interviews in general. ● Practice DSA from sites like Leetcode and GFG. (Personally I only used Leetcode because of the better interface and community) ● Solve problems from lists – there are many, but choose one that suits you. Some examples are Strivers SDE sheet, Neetcode 150, Blind 75 (there are many). Personally, I used Neetcode in the beginning but not one sheet in particular, I would just keep on solving any question I encountered. ● Practice OOPS from sites like GFG (Just message me if you want more advice regarding this) ● Practice DBMS and OS from your academic notes/presentations. They are more than enough for your interviews. Final advice Everyone does feel overwhelmed by the entire experience. But you must give priority to your health and mental well-being throughout the preparation phase, as it can be exhausting and draining. It is known that this entire phase is stressful and each batch goes through it. I have myself. Engage in activities that help you destress and unwind – do something creative to balance the logical – left brain activity. Practice some daily meditation as well, it really helps relieve stress and tension. Be happy, and enjoy this entire journey! All the best! Cheers! Sidenote: Maximum Index - My approach Okay, so if you did find an approach, great! But don’t worry if you did not… Let’s look at my observations and approach. Observation I looked at the examples and figured out 2 things: 1. The aim is to maximize the final index. 2. A step means either to “stay” at the same index or “move on”. 3. The leap I can take increases with each step. (At the 5th step my leap is of 5 indexes) 4. I cannot take a leap in which I encounter the bad index/bad element. Approach Let’s forget about the bad index for a second and just focus on the step choice. I figured that I should aim to always choose to “move on” when at a higher index, otherwise I will miss out on the opportunity of taking a giant leap. What this means is, IF I want to “stay” I should prefer to “stay” early on in the game rather than later, otherwise I will miss out on a giant leap later on. Example: Initially i=0, j=1 (according to problem statement) ● I choose to stay at 0, and j counter increases to 2 now. ● I choose to stay at 0, and the j counter increases to 3 now. ● I choose to stay at 0 again and the j counter increases to 4 now. Observe that with each choice/step, the value of j increases, and I am missing out on an opportunity to jump ‘j’ number of steps. So I should choose to “stay” only at the initial stage of the game where the stakes are low and my leap value is least (this happens when i=0, j=1). We want to keep leaping in order to maximize the final landing index. Okay so one major thing out of the way, I should “stay” ONLY IF i=0, j=1. Otherwise I won’t be maximizing the final index. So what about the bad index/bad element? I want to avoid leaping onto the bad index at any step. I can avoid this easily. Notice in the example: steps = 4 badElement = 6 The pointer is limited to 4 steps and should avoid the bad item 6. ● Scenario 1: ○ In the first step, j starts at 1. ○ Move 1 unit to index 0+1=1 and j=2. ○ At step 2, move 2 units to index 1+2-3, and j=3. ○ At step 3, do not move. Otherwise point moves 3 units to bad item 6. Now j=4. ○ At step 4, move 4 units to item 3+4=7. ● Scenario 2: ○ At step 1, remain at index 0. Now j=2. ○ At step 2, move 2 units to index 0+2-2 and j=3. ○ At step 3, move 3 units to index 2+3=5 and j=4 ○ At step 4, move 4 units to index 5+4=9 The maximum index that can be reached is 9. In scenario 1: We chose to move at step 1 itself. Then we choose to not move at step 3 since we’ll encounter the bad element, thus missing out on a leap of 3 units. 0->1->3->(stay)->3->7 In scenario 2: What if we chose to not move at step 1 itself? Now j=2. Obviously we won’t encounter the bad index=6 now, because the leap distance has changed by 1 for each step and thus we will be off by one unit. So now if we keep leaping: 0->(stay)->2->5->9. So all you have to do is, find out: max ( final index when leap at step 1, final index when stay at step 1 ) ( Final index when stay at step 1 will be ) > ( Final index when leap at step 1 ) ONLY if the bad index lies in the path of ( Final index when leap at step 1 ) and the reverse is also true.
